messages.content: *Steps echo down the halls. A reverberation shoved through the sandstone, dissipating within it, yet kept alive through reflections of its shape back into the open air. One after another. Plod. Plod. Plod. Each can be heard throughout the entire hall. There is no need to worry. It is known that he will arrive, he is growing closer.*
"Ah."
"My child."
"What a relief it is to find you, at last. We were all worried, quite so."
`"...Don't do that."`
"I am afraid I do not understand."
`"I'm not naive. Not really worth lying if it's *that* transparent."`
"...Yes, well... I was worried. These halls are quite labyrinthine. It would not be a surprise were I to learn many a wayward soul had met their end within."
`"Well, duh. That keeps most people back, at least. Just... somewhere I can hide, 'til this all blows over."`
"My child, there is no need to run and hide down within these dangerous depths. I am more than capable of officiating a mediation for whatever slight has been committed."
`"Yeah, good luck with that. Those guys don't exactly listen to reason, y'know? Yeah, yeah, I'm one to talk, and whatever, but they're scary, Father."`
"They also have a tendency to leave those not in their 'game' alone, no?"
"...How much do you owe these men?"

`"Th-that's not! It's not about the money, it's the pride! It's like, their fucking ego! I swindled them fair and square, rigging the game's part of the fun! But they- these guys are gonna fucking kill me, Father! I can't go out there!"`
"Would this be enough to satisfy these men?"
`"Th-that's... you can't sell that! Isn't it... important? For religious... stuff?"`
"It is merely a fancy trinket. The form carries meaning, not the material. If I am wrong, I am sure it will find its own way back here, do you not think? All tends to find itself linked to its home."
`"Well, uh... thanks, but... you really don't have to do that for me. I'm just being a pussy, honestly. Throw me to the wolves, it'll be... fine."`

"Those words are mere platitudes. You know it is impossible that could ever convince me. For your pain is my own. I weep learning that you still face such adversity, and yet... you seem unable to tear yourself away from activities inviting of it. Why is that, my child?"
`"...You wouldn't get it. It's just... exhilarating. Just- just for a moment, people stop looking at me like..."`

"Very well. Just keep in mind, my child, our doors are always open for volunteers. Some good could come of it, learning a bit more regarding measured empathy. Rather than these... destructive instincts you so frequently find yourself giving into."
"Follow me, I shall- NO!"
`"Just... gotta... damn!"`
"YOU... FOOLISH... Auughh... My child, you merely needed to indicate you were hindered. I am more than capable of-"
`"You didn't notice the whole... y'know, cave-in?"`
"I... noted its presence. My primary concern was focused on you, however. Have you freed your foot successfully?"
`"Yeah... hurts like a bitch, though..."`
"We shall have it treated above ground. I shall bring you there. There is no need for you to strain yourself, it shall only bring further harm to-"
`"Hey, Father? What's... up with those holes?"`
"Holes?"

`"Yeah, the... Y'know, up there. I think the cave-in might've exposed them? I didn't, uh, get a good look before it. Whole place was pretty unstable, wall came down 'fore I could process. Looks like people? Any kinda old-timey figures?"`
"I have no idea who they are. No one I recognize."

Ambient noise begins to rise in volume, ushered in through the sunrise's announcement of the morning. The noise of the guards getting to work cleaning up camp permeates the walls of the tent, as the sun's rays peek through its flaps. These two act in concert to bring an end to the slumber of all those here at roughly the same time. These tents are a temporary measure set up each night to avoid the need to remain shoved together in the wagons like a pack of sardines during the night. One for the Emperor and his right hand, one for the rest of the guards, and one for the remainder. Typically, the remainder would be entirely comprised of workers, but an exception has been made for this trip.

"Bucky" awakens next to Ace; he remains by her side even in the night. Briar McGregor is only a short distance away. This will be the last day until the convoy reaches its destination, an agreed upon meeting point with their Newark counterparts, a short distance from the town of Paradise proper.

As the natural shine of the morning light filters through my eyelids, I regain my awareness of the world around me. Of the people; of the sounds, the smells, the feeling of Ace's warmth radiating just strongly enough for me to feel it, even in these warm environs. I don't bother pretending to still be asleep; it's tempting, but none of the people around me would do it, and I'm still in the mindset of trying my very best to fit in, even in these unnoticeable ways. I yawn, stretch my arms wide, and roll over to give my old friend a quick squeeze. "Wake up, Cilly!"
I poke him in the cheek to make sure my point is made.
Slowly, I open my eyes as I feel the warmth of the sun rays. I sit up and yawn covering my mouth, looking at those around me, a little annoyed by not being able to sleep more.
Ace lethargically waves at Bucky, signaling her to stop. "I'm up. I'm uuuaauuu~" His sentence is interrupted by a yawn, as he stretches his arms out to an unseen sky.
The other workers also provide their fair share of yawns and stretches, beginning to file out of the tent.

I poke him again. "This is the last bridge of our journey, huh? I'm so... uah... I'm nervous, honestly... but we shouldn't dawdle. It's almost time for breakfast, one of the most important meals that there is!"
I hop to my feet, shaking myself off to metaphorically dispel the tiredness of the night prior.
"Are you actually up, Ace? Or are you just going to stay down there?"
He follows her lead, taking a stand after a few seconds of a thoughtful expression. "...Isn't it the most important, singular? There's... not that many total, right?"
Briar stands up slowly stretching her arms up, she giggles as she overhears the conversation while walking out of the tent.

As Briar reaches the exit, she comes face to face with Bixbite, currently on her way into the tent. Her expression is as deathly serious as ever, but mixed with something else. "McGregor." It's not entirely clear what this means.
I turn away from Bixbite instinctively, not wanting to draw any unnecessary attention.
"Well... there are a lot of meals. A lot of words for meals. I didn't want to make such a strong judgment without thinking about it more for myself."
Briar looks at her nervously "Hm- Sorry" she says quickly moving out of the way.
I quirk the side of my lips. "Brunches are usually pretty important, for instance. Special occasions that call for them, you know..."
"Um. Not really the conversation to be having right now, haha! We should get going... soon?" I glance over to see if Bixbite is still blocking the way out.

Bixbite nods, approving of Briar's understanding of the chain of authority here, before continuing inward.

Ace seems to be hanging on every one of Bucky's words. "Oh, yeah, I guess we should. Sorry, didn't mean to... sidetrack there. Just didn't want to miss any-" He's interrupted by an arm being wrapped around his upper body. Bixbite grips him tightly.

"Acilis. We need to talk." She spits out, dangerously close to his ears.

Damn it. I reach out to help Ace before remembering, once more, how important it is that I not be seen as somebody worth paying attention to. I draw my hand back lightly and shuffle awkwardly to the side. This woman... I probably just need to let her get this anger out of her system. He... he shouldn't be in any danger. It's fine.
Briar stands still by the exit, she knows she should probably leave the tent as this is none of her business but she can't deny how curious she is about what is going on.

An almost imperceptible expression of shock flashes across him as Bucky pulls her hand back, but he quickly swallows it and puts on a brave face. "We... yeah, we can talk." He glances around, noticing Briar's still here too, before turning back to Bucky. "You guys should get breakfast. I'll, uh-"

"No one's having breakfast. Not today." Bixbite interrupts him.
"There is no breakfast today?" Briar speaks surprised without thinking. She quickly covers her mouth looking at all of them nervously "Sorry, didn't mean to interrupt- I will take my leave now"

Bixbite's head limply angles itself towards Briar, staring for a moment. "...Everyone's being gathered outside. You'll see what I mean." She begins to drag a clearly terrified Ace towards the tent's exit by his shirt collar.
I shrink into myself, the words coming out of my mouth before I can stop them. "I'm... I'm sorry, but could you please... be a bit more gentle with him...? He hasn't done anything wrong."
She stops in her tracks, and speaks without breaking her gaze from the exit. "And whose judgement is that?"
"Ah... well..."
I go silent, my cheeks burning.
With a anxious heart, Briar quickly runs out the exit escaping the situation and looking to see what she meant outside.

"That's what I thought. You're no Hero, and you're certainly no Reaper. You don't have what it takes to understand the sins of this world, not even those of your friend here." She drags him out, handling him a bit more rough than before, following after Briar.
I hurry after them, maintaining a healthy distance.

There's a crowd gathered outside. It's not an orderly one, but rather suddenly formed through confusion and curiosity. In its center sits the emperor atop a makeshift throne of shattered crates and scattered goods. It's as if a tornado had struck a singular spot in the camp, targeting all of their supplies.

The emperor, separated from the crowd by his guards, sighs from behind his signature avian mask. His head is currently propped up by a fist, clearly denoting boredom. "What took you so long, Bixxy? ...eheheheheh, let's get this show started, how about we?"

A show? I... surely it's not one that involves Ace, right? What does he have to do with this? What's going on?? We were so close... so close to making it, to reaching the end of our journey, together and in one piece... what did I do wrong? Where did I slip up? No, no... I didn't. I haven't made any mistakes. This is not some grand reveal of what I've involved him in. I'm being paranoid. I'm assuming the worst, which is not what has ever been or will ever be helpful, conducive to good thinking. Be measured, Mari. Ace will forgive you for not striding up to save him like some hero.
I take a few deep breaths. Wait and see. Steady thoughts.
What sin could he have committed? He's not exactly the most adventurous guy. Stealing a bit of extra food? Ticking off the wrong engineer? What was it?
Briar looks at the scene and pouts. "I'm really hungry..." she whispers at herself a little annoyed and confused

Bixbite tosses Ace past the crowd, right at the foot of the Emperor's pile. It takes him a second to move, but he manages to sit up, positioning himself on his knees. He stares at the Emperor, scared and confused.

"...Ace. That is your preferred name, right? Quite the high opinion you have, there. The ace what? Ace construction worker? You don't really look the part." The emperor hops down, and leans over Ace, examining him through the eyes of his mask. "Quite scrawny for this line of work. Runt of the litter? Overcompensating? How male egos do hunger."

"I... I don't... What's happening?" Ace is on the verge of tears.

It really, really hurts to see him like this. I know Ace... he wouldn't hurt a fly! This is sickening. But... what can I do? What could I do to help, even if I were here for less important reasons? It's the emperor! He has every man here on his side, working for his protection. I... I just have to trust that they wouldn't put on a performance like this if they were going to do something too bad to him. They know that would be demoralizing. That's all this is, a verbal warning, for... whatever it is. It's fine. It's fine.
I clench and unclench my fists a few times.

"Oh? Was that not clear? Let me spell it out, then. I am the Emperor, this is my court, and this is your trial." He retrieves a dagger from inside his coat. "Or, more straight to the point, your execution."

Ace's face drains of all color.
Briar gasps covering her mouth. She feels like she should intervene but there is no way she has the courage for that.
I suddenly get dizzy. What? What? What are they talking about? Why would... I... they...

I... I don't care anymore. The plan doesn't matter. This is my friend, Ace. I stumble towards the 'throne', shouting out at the lounging ruler. "Wait! Wait! H-he hasn't done anything! What's the crime?! You have to tell us!"

"...eheheheh... Mayyybe you should look in front of you, Bucks. We have a witness who saw him sneaking out on his own last night, and this morning, well..." He gestures to the pile of destruction he was making use of. "Our supplies are in a bit of a rough shape. Without any food, we're gonna staaaaarve. So I had Bixxy here find an alternative source of protein." He ruffles Ace's hair.

"I-I don't understand! How could he have possibly done all of this on his own? This destruction... if it was already like this when you found it, then that's a huge undertaking! It looks like a bomb went off... sir... and you yourself just called him scrawny. Do you really believe that he's the one to blame?"

I look out at the crowd, then back at the emperor. "We've all had to... you know... let it leak a little before, right? We're hardly prisoners in our own tent... I know that you're not going to let all of these people live in fear of retribution for something as simple as that, right? Would that really be good for... productivity?"
I'm trying to appeal to his best interests.

"Oh, you *are* a funny one, aren't you? I'd rather they live in fear than not live at all. I'm just looking out for my subjects, and a substitute has to be found for our lost goods, riiiight?" He twirls his dagger. "Would you rather us starve? His death will be for the good of everyone. We'll harvest him for our growth."
I yell out at the crowd. "Everyone here... please raise your hand if you would be willing to eat my friend Ace here for breakfast! His meat!" I gesture at him shakily.
Please, nobody actually do it... be reasonable...
Briar speaks up scared. Her words are full of stutters." I think we need to calm down-, this is something I don't think anybody wants-"
I smile at her gratefully. "Yes! See! We can work on other solutions. We have... so many brilliant people here, so many bright folks with skills that can be put towards finding a better way."

The rest of the workers all hold expressions of varying levels of discomfort, fear, and nausea. Even the guards are starting to look a bit concerned. No one raises their hand except Bixbite.

"...eheheheheeeeehhh. And so she ran crying to her friends for help. How trite. Let's see how that serves you." The emperor shrugs and shakes his head. "Put your hand down Bixxy, you know he's innocent. I had my guards set up this little stage during the night, seemed like a fun way to announce we're out of rations."
"Wh-what?!"
Briars mouth drops to the ground and her face turns a bright red "T-That isn't very funny sir!"

This was all some sort of... sick joke? I exposed myself... showed my face to every single fucking worker here for nothing? I suddenly realize how furious I am. Calm down. Calm down. This is- this means that everything is okay. You made a mistake, but it wasn't your fault. It wasn't anybody's fault. This is how it was going to play out. Everything is okay.

"I... thank you, your highness. For letting us enjoy this spectacle. It was truly... shocking." I bow to him, and then walk with slow steps back to the tent, not saying another word or making eye contact with Ace.
I can't stop my hands from shaking on the way there, though.

"Maybe not *very* funny, but still, like, pretty funny." The emperor pulls a cylinder out from his coat, and tosses it down to Ace. "Here, the last can of beans, for your trouble."

Still looking completely out of it, Ace silently grabs it and scrambles to his feet, following after Bucky.
((If Briar doesn't follow we'll split channels))
Worried and upset she turns away from the emperor and follows behind Ace and Bucky to talk to them.

The three of them are in the tent alone, the rest of the crowd beginning to disperse elsewhere in the camp. Ace is still pale, but recovering slightly. "Th-that- I- I- I mean- that was scary! I couldn't... I mean, thank you, Mari. Even if it, uh, wasn't..." He hasn't noticed Briar behind him.

I grab the can of beans from Ace and pry them open. "Yeah... that was scary..." I scoop out a handful and throw them into my mouth. "Hopefully he doesn't pull anything like that again anytime soon. What an... well, you know. Not to put too fine a point on it or anything."
Chew.

As the lid of the can is pried open, a spring shoots forth towards Bucky's face. Its base is attached to the bottom of the can, and the top of the spring is adorned with a miniature figure dressed in the Emperor's garb. There's still some beans in the center of the spring.
"Gah!" I bat it away. It stays stuck in place, obviously.
She walks up to them and asks "are you okay? That was horrible! He is so rude" she crosses her arms annoyed
"Ugh... yeah, I'm fine. Thank you..." I smile weakly up at her, although I'm a bit confused on why she's still so interested in us after the whole trial thing turned out to be a non-issue.
"Do you... work here, or something?"

Ace nods at Bucky "I-I guess we're fine, then? Yeah, uh..." He eyes the mini-monarch warily for a few moments. "She's definitely not one of the hires. Some of the boys and I have been, you know, uh, theorizing why she's here... I guess..." He suddenly remembers the person he's talking about is in the room, and turns to Briar nervously. "N-not in a bad way! Just... you don't really see... people tagging along, like this. Uh."
I roll my eyes. "As tactful as ever, Ace."
She nods and smiles "I'm just traveling with everyone!"
"I'm trying to visit my brother and I'm very excited! It's my first traveling ever" she starts talking rapidly with excitement

"Oh! Well, I mean... that's admirable." I think for a second. "I'm a bit confused, though. Is your brother, like... one of the people living in the village that we're about to, um..." I choose my words carefully. "The village that we're going to be working in?"

"I didn't realize that anybody currently in Paradise was related to a family from the outside world." It's a strange thing to think about. The emperor, doing this to people who are, in a sense, his own subjects... but I guess I should have come to expect such cruelty from that deviant.
"He is a very important person in Newark!" She looks around thinking "I actually don't know much about these places..."
"everything around me is so new to me"

"Ohh... I see. I just..." A flash of guilt crosses my face for a second. "I'm sorry that you have to spend so long with us, I guess. Even if everything goes to plan... we're a long way from Newark. I hope you're ready for a long haul."
I hand her the can of beans.
Ace silently listens. He looks to have pretty much recovered, but shares an expression of guilt for much longer than Bucky.
What does he have to be guilty about? I mentally scoff.
"yes! I'm excited for this trip, it's okay" her smile shines brightly
"Yeah... me too. I suppose I'm excited too." I smile back. "Here's to this beautiful and forgiving world that we live in."

The morning passes, a tragedy having successfully been avoided, due to never having been a possibility from the start. They'll consider it a practice run for what's to come.

The guards and workers finish cleaning up the camp. The tents come down, the mules are reattached to the carriages, and the precarious pile is left to weather the arid desert. The convoy resumes its journey to Paradise.

A few hours of travel pass peacefully. Briar, Bucky, and Ace are no longer alone, but share a carriage with a handful of other workers packed in alongside them. It appears that an awkward silence in the conversation weighs a bit too much on Ace, and he speaks up.

"S-so... how about this weather, huh?" The sky is perfectly clear.

I genuinely consider the question. Ace doesn't deserve to be brushed off. I'm glad he's still here to ask me mundane things. I'm glad he's still here.
"Well, I do appreciate the cover we have from the desert sun. It's admittedly a bit too warm for me. Back at home, I... I always had better ways to keep cool, if I wanted to."
"Do you have any water on you, speaking of?"
Briar sighs and moves her sleeves up her arms "Its so hot here... I will need to purchase some short sleeve shirts later"

"I think, uh, the water was included, in the, you know, things they accused me of-" The carriage is flung backwards, tumbling over itself. A deafening crack fills the ears of everyone present. Wood fractures, the mules whimper in pain, and the passengers are flung around, upside down and back again as their anchor to the ground comes loose. Chunks of broken wood fly at them as the carriage falls apart around them, bruising and drawing blood as a few of the workers narrowly avoid full on impalement. It comes to a stop after a few seconds, kicking up a cloud of dust.
I- what? I suddenly realize that I'm on my back. "Gh- what the bell? What happened?!"
I try pulling myself up to my feet, but it's painful... I cough a few times, breathing in the dust.
Is there anything around that it looks like we, um, ran into?
"Ouch..." Briar cried as she laid face down after the impact, she just stayed where she was only moving her face to look at those around her trying to see what happened

No carriage seems to have survived unscathed. The path is filled with broken wood, and scattered bodies. Most passengers seem to be struggling to move, while a few lie limp. The mules haven't fared much better.

Bixbite stands tall, lifting The Emperor from the wreckage. He supports his weight on her, and begins muttering. "Damn it... too early... I thought we'd time, timed... better..." He looks over the crowd and raises his voice. "STAY CALM! STAY... just... grab... grab onto something..."

I doubt the emperor really knows what he's talking about when it comes to desert threats, honestly, or whatever he's implying. Sheltered brat. But I internally roll my eyes and glance around to see what the nearest thing I can grab is anyways. A plank of wood, maybe?
"You okay, guys? Ace? Uh, other girl? I don't think I know your name. Sorry."
"I'm over here" she lifts up one of her arms waving her hand "Briar is my name... can you help me?" she looks at them with blood coming down her forhead

"Oh, geez, um... you might need something, yeah. A bandage, maybe." After selecting my requisite board, I start carefully picking my way over the rubble to reach her. I make a mental note of her name. Briar. A plant with thorns... I wonder if she has any edge to her, or if her soft appearance is closer to telling the truth.

"I-I'm fith... ptheh..." Ace spits some sand out of his mouth as he lifts himself up to his knees. Holding his head, he stares at something in the distance, past The Emperor. "Um... guys... you might, uh, want to see this."

A massive sandstorm is approaching in the distance, a low rumbling sound announcing its impending arrival.
I don't look back at whatever he's talking about. Helping the girl is my priority. I'm here to help people, regardless of the form it takes at the moment. "Does that wound hurt, Briar?"
She nods slowly with tears in her eyes "it does..."

"GET DOWN, IDIOTS!" The Emperor yells out to them as the storm, approaching at unnatural speed, consumes the group. Wood is flung through the air, but the wind isn't quite strong enough to lift a person, just to knock them down. Sand continuously slams against bare skin and open wounds as the wind rushes past their ears, nearly drowning out the screams.

I start pinwheeling my arms, already barely balanced on these mounds of rubble *without* them moving around underneath me. "Shit! Shit!" I fall backwards roughly, ending up on my knees with my beam above my head as a kind of makeshift shield, trying my best to stop the wind from pulling it out of my grasp.
Briar sighs and stays laying on the ground moving her hands to her head trying to protect herself

The Emperor continues to yell, barely audible. "STAND YOUR GROUND! THE STORM WILL PASS, WE JUST NEED TO- AUUUGGHhhhhh...!" It hits The Emperor first, but quickly, the ground underneath the whole group splits open, the sand shifting, forming new hills and deep trenches.

The group is separated, and with the storm blocking their vision, no one can see where their comrades went.
Briar tumbles down a sandy slope, vision fully obscured.
She closes her eyes terrified, this is far from what she expected from this trip. As she tumbles all she can do is to hope for the best.

As she continues to tumble, Briar suddenly feels something wrap itself around her body like a snake. Before she can process it, the thick thread tightens around her, and her movement jerks to the side. She's no longer heading straight down, instead being dragged elsewhere.
"wow, okay its over" she thinks to herself, there is no point to trying to free herself really and she has no plans on opening her eyes to see what is the thing that may be taking her to her demise

After about half a minute, the sandstorm lets up. It seems she was dragged outside of it by something. "You got in a real mess back there, missy. How'd ya go and get caught up in somethin' like that?" It's an unfamiliar voice.
fear leaves her body almost immediately as she opens her eyes to look towards where the voice came from with curiosity.

A tan-skinned man stares down at her. His lengthy hair is jet-black hair is flowing in the wind. His eyes are sunken, but his orange irises glow through his exhaustion. He's sporting a thick beard and a leather jacket, a sheriff's badge affixed to the lapel. In his hands, he's gripping a rope, currently tied into a lasso around Briar's body.
She blinks multiple times just taking in his appearance "T-Thank you" she stutters after a long silence from her part

He leans down and unties the rope. "You're lucky I saw your group on patrol. Coulda been real bad if you stayed in that cloud." Reaching into his satchel, he pulls out a bottle, and motions to her forehead. "Now this might sting a little but town's a bit off, so we don't wanna leave that wound untreated, alright?"
She nods and smiles brightly, all those romance novels with similar scenarios passing through her head before coming back to reality "Y-Yeah thats fine, thank you for saving me!"
"Now that's a surprise. Quite the positive attitude you got after all that." He wets a rag with the bottle's contents, and wipes down her wound. It does, in fact, sting.
She closes her eyes and bites her lip as it stings. When he is done she slowly stands up and brushes off the dirt in her dress even though that doesn't get close to making it look clean at all.

After packing away the bottle and rag, he calmly glances around. "...Ever ridden a horse before? I left my steed behind when I saw the storm. Old girl's not made for those conditions. Should still be nearby, she doesn't scare easily."
Briar stares at him with a nervous expression as she slowly shakes her head "Never..."
"Hm. Alright, just hold onto me, then. I'll keep her steady." He sets off in a direction away from the remnants of the storm.
Her face turns a slight red as scenarios start passing through her brain, she has definitely read too many romance novels. She quickly follows behind him with a smile and her eyes shining.

The two come across a horse before long. The mare's dark tail sways in the wind, and her brown coat matches her owner's jacket. He strokes her neck gently as he reaches her. "Good girl. Gonna need you to carry a bit more weight than usual... but still pretty light." He turns to Briar and motions to the horse's saddle. "Need a hand gettin' up?"
She nods rapidly and walks close to the horse "Thank you so much again! I don't know what would have happened to me if you weren't there" but concern appears in her face "I hope my friends are okay"

He hesitates for a moment, choosing his words carefully. "...That group looked tough. I only saw from a distance, but it seemed like soldiers and laborers. They should've been trained for this." He scratches his head. "Well, not sure 'bout that bird-looking fellow. Never seen that before."
Shivers run through her back at the mention of the emperor "Yeah... he is such a weird person, he scares me a little bit"

The man places an arm around her back, and proceeds to lift her in a bridal carry. He takes a couple of seconds to get a steady foothold, and lifts her on the back of the horse. "There ya go. Nice and easy."
Briar's face turns a bright red "T-Thank you" she stutters as she covers half her face with one of her hands. She looks down at the horse a little nervous
The horse seems to be horse shaped, upon further inspection. The man lifts himself onto the horse as well, positioned in front of Briar. He takes the reins in his hands. "Y'all ready?"
"I think I'm ready" she says quietly, grabbing onto him as the horse starts moving.
"Giddy up, girl!" The horse starts its brisk trot back to civilization. All the while carrying its owner on its back, along with the girl attached to him around the waist.
((End session))

After a brief journey, expediated by a particularly well-bred horse, a town begins to come into view as Briar and company pass over the crest of a sand dune. It's fairly small, with quaint wooden buildings scattered throughout. Three distinct structures punctuate it, seeming somewhat out of place. A higher class mansion surrounded by a garden on one end, a structure constructed out of some sort of stone on the other, and a golden statue extending towards the sky in the middle.

"There it is. Paradise. I know, I know, didn't pick the name myself."
Briar looks at the structures with wonder in her eyes "It looks so cool!" she exclaims and points at the garden in specific
"Heh. If you like it that much... 'spose I can give you a tour. That's the mayor's garden, tends to it herself. Not much else to do 'round these parts."
"Yes please! I would love to see it"

He nods, and goes silent for a moment. His voice takes a more stern tone once he finds his words. "We might have trouble. Looks like your group weren't the only ones rolling into our little town." He begins directing the horse towards two figures near the stone structure.
She grabs onto him tightly as she looks at the figures a little nervous.
He brings his steed to a halt as it reaches the figures.
Mari tumbles down a sandy slope, vision fully obscured.
"Waughhhhh!" My arms go spinning in a blur as I try and fail to tuck myself into a smaller ball. I'm going to die. This is it. I'm going to fucking die. All for nothing. Fuck.

I think briefly about whether I should have done more with my life. I could have spent more time with Ace... or maybe started making nice with the cute girl earlier in the trip. I don't know. I'm not sure what I would have changed, or when. Probably things went wrong way before then. I just have the sense that my life hadn't really started yet. Any now my chance gets wasted on some fucking sand.
I get back to spinning.
